headline: US offers Russia Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine for the first time
dek: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the proposal] The US has officially approached Russia with a proposal to provide Ukraine with security guarantees similar to NATO Articles 4 and 5 (consultations + collective defence), Politico reported citing two senior US administration officials; the Financial Times…
sources: Senior US administration officials, Monday briefing for journalists (on condition of attribution to US officials only); Politico, Financial Times, PBS
fault_line: Article 5 for a non-member -- a US-backed guarantee that looks like NATO membership without the membership: real protection for Kyiv, or a promise Moscow will never accept?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the proposal] The US has officially approached Russia with a proposal to provide Ukraine with security guarantees similar to NATO Articles 4 and 5 (consultations + collective defence), Politico reported citing two senior US administration officials; the Financial Times reports a US official put the same 'Article 5-like' guarantee to Moscow, with any final decision resting with Trump. PBS (via UNN) reports the same from a US official. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the briefing] In a Monday briefing for journalists, US officials said the aim in Abu Dhabi is to start the 'final end' to the war and establish a regular rhythm of negotiations; session 1 covers ceasefire monitoring + arrangements stopping either side using a pause to rearm; session 2 covers territory. The US also floated easing sanctions on Russia in stages, with automatic reimposition if Moscow breaks an agreement, and reviving the NATO-Russia Council (suspended 2022) as a de-escalation channel. Rubio called security guarantees the main topic. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the limits] Whether the US itself would offer such a guarantee is for Trump to decide; officials said Trump has been clear Europe should carry the financial burden. No deadline for a final agreement or a leaders' meeting. [CONTEXT] Russia wants all of Donetsk; Kyiv wants the current line of contact as the boundary. Moscow's response to the guarantee proposal is not on record; Politico notes Moscow's agreement is unlikely.
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct tiered publisher families: Politico (T2, via 1news.az carry) + Financial Times (T2, via Turkiye Today carry) + PBS (T2, via UNN carry) + ANI (T1, via Tribune India / Deccan Chronicle carries).
sections.what_disputed: (a) Single origin: every family traces to the same Monday US-officials' briefing / senior officials -- multi-family carry of one source, not independent confirmation of Moscow's position. (b) No Russian response on record; Politico itself notes Moscow's agreement is unlikely since the proposal implies preserving Western military support for Ukraine. (c) The guarantee is a proposal, not a commitment: Trump has not decided, and no text exists. (d) Peskov said the talks would take place without European representatives (UNN), while US officials want Europeans in a wider format -- a format dispute, not a settled structure.
sections.why_matters: For the first time, Washington has officially asked Moscow to accept an Article 5-like guarantee for Ukraine -- NATO-level protection without NATO membership. Trump hasn't decided whether America itself would give it, and Moscow hasn't answered. The guarantee is the whole ballgame in Abu Dhabi -- and it exists only as an ask.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (first publications 00:18-02:16 ; not recorded) -- US offers Russia Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine for the first time; staged sanctions relief + NATO-Russia Council revival on the table

totw_analysis: Our read: For the first time, Washington has officially asked Moscow to accept an Article 5-like guarantee for Ukraine -- NATO-level protection without NATO membership. Trump hasn't decided whether America itself would give it, and Moscow hasn't answered. The guarantee is the whole ballgame in Abu Dhabi -- and it exists only as an ask. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Article 5 for a non-member -- a US-backed guarantee that looks like NATO membership without the membership: real protection for Kyiv, or a promise Moscow will never accept?
